clue.text: Being airily cold, medic with pride ignoring hospital

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the abbreviation for hospital is dropped from the word for pride

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
haughtiness is arrogant pride
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor so proud he snubs the hospital, and comes across as frosty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airily cold' sounds like aloof manners, but it means literally full of draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtiness is the quality of a room exposed to chilly currents of moving air.

clue.text: Bush always has new flower coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: AY is an old word for ever or always
a bud is a flower just forming

explanation.surface: A shrub that always produces fresh blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like a plant, but it is George W. Bush, whose Texan nickname echoed his middle initial W.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubya was the popular nickname of US president George W. Bush, from the drawled pronunciation of his initial.

clue.text: Funny picture of queen touring one vast room

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so the queen's name wraps around the number

blocks.note: Queen Anne reigned in the early 1700s
I is the Roman numeral for one
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A comic painting of a queen visiting a great hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' suggests a painting, but it is a film: Woody Allen's Oscar-winning comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Hall is Woody Allen's 1977 comedy film, and a film is often called a picture.

clue.text: Conceive and develop grand car

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
an estate is a car with a long rear load space, a station wagon

explanation.surface: An engineer designing and building a large car.
explanation.definitionFit: To gestate an idea is to form it in the mind and let it mature over time, like a pregnancy.

clue.text: Hat-wearing convict shows cultivation

indicators.note: something wearing a hat has it on top, so the hat word goes around the convict

blocks.note: tile is old slang for a hat
an old lag is a habitual prisoner

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a hat demonstrates his skill at farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the preparing and working of land for growing crops.

clue.text: Reporter’s experiences with tech titan’s features upgrades

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so the next word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to know something is to have experienced it
Steve Jobs co-founded Apple

explanation.surface: A journalist's lived experience alongside a magazine profile of a tech billionaire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' looks like articles by the reporter, but it means parts of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose jobs are cosmetic surgery operations that improve the look of a facial part.

clue.text: Police ops in Escort stuck between Sierras

indicators.note: something stuck between two things sits inside them, with one on each side

blocks.note: Sierra is S in the NATO alphabet, and there are two
to escort someone on a date is to take them out

explanation.surface: Undercover detectives in a Ford Escort wedged between two Ford Sierras.
explanation.walkthrough: The Escort and the Sierra were both popular Ford cars, which is what the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakeouts are covert surveillance operations in which officers watch a place for a long time.

clue.text: Feeling less sun, ultimately, by dark shade

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of sun
umber is a dark brown pigment

explanation.surface: Getting less sunshine in the dark shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as numb-er, not as a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Number is the comparative of numb, describing something with less sensation than before.

clue.text: Skeleton crew abandoning steam ship

indicators.note: when a group abandons a place it leaves, so those letters are removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: a crew is a team
taken as written
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A skeleton crew deserting a steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skeleton crew' reads as a phrase, but Skeleton alone is the definition; TEAM leaves STEAM to give S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough outline, the bare framework of a plan, as a skeleton is.

clue.text: Pope in religious headgear saving face

indicators.note: saving here means except, so the word is taken except its front, or face

blocks.note: a turban is worn by Sikh men for religious reasons

explanation.surface: A pope in an unusual hat avoiding embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving face' means keeping one's dignity, but here it means except the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban was the papal name of eight popes, including Urban II, who launched the First Crusade.

clue.text: Words when flogging dog on short, damaged leash

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes
damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
to dog someone is to follow or stalk them

explanation.surface: Someone whipping a dog that is on a short, broken leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogging' suggests beating the dog, but in British slang it means selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales talk is the persuasive patter a seller uses, and flogging is informal British for selling.

clue.text: Work hard — live off investing say

indicators.note: to invest something is to put it inside, so the word for say is placed within the others

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
to aver is to state firmly
a player who is off is away

explanation.surface: Advice to toil and live off your investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' looks like putting money to work, but it means placing one word inside the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To beaver away is to toil steadily and industriously, like a beaver building its dam.

clue.text: Attend thrash

blocks.note: first sense: read as two words
second sense: to thrash is to hit hard or defeat soundly

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits as BE AT, which is what attending means.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent is to defeat them heavily, and to beat someone is to strike them repeatedly.

clue.text: Recall European president making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback runs the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
Jimmy Carter was a US president

explanation.surface: Remembering a European president who returned to power.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace one's steps or thoughts is to go back over them in the memory.

clue.text: Revolving fan hits me, possibly one supplying air

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the word for fan is turned back to front
possibly signals one of several arrangements of the preceding words

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spinning electric fan strikes me, perhaps the one blowing air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like the breeze from the fan, but it means a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunesmith is a songwriter, someone who provides melodies, and an air is a tune.

clue.text: Speaker no longer in seaside town

blocks.note: ex means former
a mouth is a spokesperson

explanation.surface: A former Speaker of the House retired to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The former marker comes first even though no longer follows Speaker in the clue. Exmouth is a resort on the Devon coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exmouth is a coastal resort town in Devon, at the mouth of the River Exe.

clue.text: Poet concerned with the main races on island

blocks.note: the main is the open sea, and marine means relating to it
the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A poet writing about the sea and sailing regattas on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Filippo Tommaso Marinetti was the Italian writer who founded Futurism with his 1909 manifesto.

clue.text: Residence bordering uncovered land, maybe plain

indicators.note: something bordering another surrounds it, so the residence goes round
uncovered means with its outer layer removed, so only the inside letters stay

blocks.note: a villa is a large house
the inner letters of land

explanation.surface: A house bounded by open countryside, perhaps flat ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a noun for flat land, but it is the adjective meaning unadorned.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla means ordinary or unadorned, because vanilla is the most basic ice-cream flavour.

clue.text: Musician in classical sextet having time after encore

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
bis is called out to ask for an encore
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A musician in a chamber sextet gets extra time after an encore.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibist is a vibraphone player, a percussionist in jazz or orchestral music.

clue.text: Nation somehow succeeded, or chooses to succeed

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters fall into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A country managed to prosper, or it picks a successor.
explanation.definitionFit: To anoint someone is to pick them as heir, from the oil used in consecrating kings.

clue.text: Bob respectfully agreed to return after lacking politeness

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for agreed is reversed

blocks.note: curt means rudely brief
yes signals agreement

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob respectfully consented to come back after being rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a name, but it means a small bending movement.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtsey is to bob down by bending the knees, a woman's traditional gesture of respect.

clue.text: Spirited criminal getting life? That’s about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for life goes around the letter for right

blocks.note: a con is a convict
a bio is a short life story
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A criminal receives a life sentence, and someone remarks that it is just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting life' looks like a prison sentence; life is a biography here.
explanation.definitionFit: Con brio is an Italian musical direction meaning with vigour and liveliness.

clue.text: Southern Arab state imprisons spineless supporters

indicators.note: to imprison is to hold inside, so the country's name surrounds the letter

blocks.note: Yemen is a country in the Arabian Peninsula
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A southern Arabian country jails its weak-willed followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who agree with a superior on everything rather than risk dissent.

clue.text: Out-of-work cleric’s error

indicators.note: out of means without, so the following word is taken out of the cleric

blocks.note: a bishop is a senior clergyman
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An unemployed vicar's mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-work' reads as jobless, but it splits into a removal instruction and the thing removed. Bish is informal British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bish is a dated British colloquialism for a mistake or slip-up, as in making a bish.

clue.text: Formerly tender poet attacked from behind

indicators.note: from behind means starting at the back, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: Ezra Pound was an American poet
to be set on is to be attacked

explanation.surface: A poet who was once gentle got mugged from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like gentle, but means legal tender, money. Britain's pound note was withdrawn in 1988, replaced by a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pound notes were paper currency, legal tender in Britain until the coin replaced them.

clue.text: Briefly, leader is confident but not tense

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so one letter for tense is taken away

blocks.note: someone who trusts is confident in another
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A short-lived chief is self-assured yet relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' looks like an abbreviation signal, but it belongs to the definition: Liz Truss was UK prime minister for only 49 days in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Liz Truss led the Conservative Party and the British government for a famously short time.

clue.text: See 5
One with craft refined his ability around November

indicators.note: refined means reworked and improved, so the letters are rearranged
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the November letter

blocks.note: power is ability
November is N in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A craftsman honed his skills over the autumn month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests skill, but means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipowner possesses vessels, and craft is a general word for boats or ships.

clue.text: Colour video frames for all to see

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so the video word goes around the letter

blocks.note: a videotape, or tape
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A colour film rated suitable for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frames' suggests film stills, but it means surrounds. A U certificate marks a British film fit for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a brownish-grey shade, named from the French for mole.

clue.text: Many a report of spirits finally soaring entertains people in party

definitions.note: singular 'many a' phrasing standing for a plural answer

indicators.note: finally points at the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of soaring
to host is to entertain guests
Tories are members of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Spirits rising high as the host entertains guests at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' and 'party' suggest drinks; spirits are ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghost stories are tales recounting encounters with phantoms, and many claim to report real sightings.
